title: ESLint 8.57.1 is end-of-life and uses the legacy config format
description: LOW-1: ui/package.json declares eslint ^8.35.0, resolved to 8.57.1 — the final 8.x release, and the 8.x line is end-of-life. Dev-only, so it never reaches the shipped bundle. The upgrade is blocked by config format: ui/.eslintrc.cjs and ui/.eslintignore are legacy eslintrc, while ESLint 9 requires flat config, and @vue/eslint-config-typescript ^12.0.0 and eslint-plugin-vue ^9.9.0 must move to flat-config-aware majors.
recommendation: Migrate to ESLint 9 flat config (eslint.config.js), upgrading @vue/eslint-config-typescript and eslint-plugin-vue in the same change.

title: Weak Cognito password policy, optional MFA, and USER_PASSWORD_AUTH enabled
description: MEDIUM-9: infra/lib/constructs/auth.ts:56-62 sets a password policy of minLength 8 with requireSymbols: false; :64 sets mfa: Mfa.OPTIONAL so MFA is never enforced despite the client implementing the SMS_MFA/SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA challenge path; :71-74 enables authFlows.userPassword alongside userSrp, so the plaintext-password flow transmits passwords to the Cognito API where SRP alone would not.
recommendation: Raise minLength to 12 and set requireSymbols: true, move MFA to REQUIRED (or enforce enrolment for premium accounts), and disable authFlows.userPassword after verifying the client uses SRP.

title: Unused second HTTP stack, three validation implementations, hand-maintained service mock
description: MEDIUM-14: Three overlapping redundancies. (1) Two HTTP stacks: Apollo (ui/src/config/apollo.ts:13-19) sends a bare `authorization` header while axios (ui/src/shared/services/httpClient.ts:22-25) sends `Bearer ${token}`; httpClient has zero non-test consumers — its only importer is ui/src/shared/services/integration.test.ts — so the second stack, the axios production dependency and axios-mock-adapter exist solely for that one test. (2) Three validation implementations: the zod-backed ui/src/shared/composables/useValidation.ts plus two hand-written reimplementations (ui/src/lib/auth/composables/useFormValidation.ts, ui/src/features/profile/composables/useProfileValidation.ts). (3) ui/src/lib/auth/services/__mocks__/cognitoService.ts is a 261-LOC hand-maintained mirror of the untested 435-LOC real service, so nothing detects drift.
recommendation: Delete httpClient.ts and its test, and drop the axios/axios-mock-adapter dependencies. Consolidate validation onto the zod-backed helper, and replace the hand-written cognitoService mock with generated or type-checked test doubles.

title: grantReadWrite on the whole media bucket instead of a per-user prefix
description: LOW-11: infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:138 grants the profile-photo Lambda grantReadWrite over the entire media bucket, although the handler only ever writes under the users/<sub>/ prefix. A bug in that single function therefore has bucket-wide blast radius.
recommendation: Replace the bucket-wide grant with a prefix-scoped grant (grantReadWrite(fn, 'users/*')) matching the keys the handler actually uses.

title: no-explicit-any disabled — 31 unenforced `any` annotations
description: LOW-2: ui/.eslintrc.cjs:20 disables @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any. 31 `any` type annotations follow, 29 of them inside ui/src/lib/auth/ — the least-tested, highest-risk area: cognitoService.ts (9), CognitoAuth.vue (9), useCognitoAuth.ts (6), createRouterGuard.ts (3), errorMessages.ts (2), plus infra/lib/lambda/profile-photo/index.ts (2). Feature code under ui/src/features/ is any-free and uses `error: unknown` correctly.
recommendation: Re-enable no-explicit-any with a scoped override for ui/src/lib/auth/, then replace the `any` annotations with concrete SDK types or `unknown` and remove the override.

title: Hardcoded demo credentials seeded by default and emitted as a plaintext CloudFormation output
description: HIGH-1: infra/lib/kirofit-stack.ts:76-78 defaults a seeded demo user to demo@kirofit.dev / WorkshopDemo1! with tier=premium, enabled whenever environment !== 'production' (:69-75). The plaintext password is published as the DemoUserPassword CloudFormation output (:91-95) and passed as a custom-resource property set with admin_set_user_password(Permanent=True) (infra/lib/constructs/seed-user.ts:15-21, 119-123). The same credential pair is duplicated in Makefile:14,16,52-57 and README.md:100-101,110. The stack always provisions a public CloudFront distribution, so any non-production deployment is an internet-reachable premium account with known credentials.
recommendation: Remove the credential defaults; require explicit context values or generate a random password stored in Secrets Manager. Never emit the password as a CloudFormation output or print it from the Makefile, and strip the pair from README.md.

title: Lambda runtime pinned to the outdated nodejs20.x managed runtime
description: HIGH-4: infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:129 pins the profile-photo NodejsFunction to lambda.Runtime.NODEJS_20_X. Node.js 20 has left active support and will reach end of Lambda managed-runtime support ahead of newer lines; nodejs24.x is the current managed runtime.
recommendation: Raise the runtime to lambda.Runtime.NODEJS_24_X and address any Lambda RIC / Node 24 breaking changes in infra/lib/lambda/profile-photo/index.ts.

title: CloudFront Function generated as an inline JS string with a fault-injection kill switch
description: MEDIUM-13: infra/lib/constructs/ui-hosting.ts:68-122 builds the CloudFront viewer-request Function by string-concatenating JavaScript with ${kvsId} interpolated into it. The generated code is never type-checked, linted or unit-tested, uses legacy `var`, swallows key-value-store errors into a silent fallback (:76-80), and contains a fault-injection kill switch returning HTTP 503 (:112-114) that can be triggered for a named release in production.
recommendation: Move the function body into a real source file bundled from disk so it is type-checked, linted and unit-tested, and gate or remove the fault-injection path for production.

title: Triple-duplicated test suites with six copies of the same mock bootstrap
description: LOW-7: Each covered service has three overlapping suites — exerciseService.test.ts (125 LOC) + .unit.test.ts (431) + .property.test.ts (267), and profileService.test.ts (138) + .unit.test.ts (316) + .property.test.ts (158). The .test/.unit.test pairs overlap substantially and the identical `getToken: () => 'mock-token'` harness is duplicated six times (exerciseService.test.ts:14, .unit.test.ts:17, .property.test.ts:13, profileService.test.ts:7, .unit.test.ts:16, .property.test.ts:42).
recommendation: Merge each overlapping .test/.unit.test pair into a single suite (preserving all distinct assertions) and extract the shared mock bootstrap into one test helper imported by all suites.

title: Deprecated exports still shipped and two unimplemented TODOs
description: LOW-8: Two deprecated symbols are still exported and shipped — ui/src/lib/preferences/types.ts:67 ("@deprecated Use MyPreferencesQueryResult instead") and ui/src/lib/preferences/graphql/operations.ts:34 ("@deprecated Use GET_MY_PREFERENCES instead"). Two TODOs remain unimplemented at ui/src/features/profile/services/profileService.ts:270 and :281. No FIXME/HACK/XXX comments exist and there is no commented-out production code beyond two lines of Cypress scaffolding.
recommendation: Migrate the remaining callers to the replacement symbols and remove the deprecated exports; implement the two profile-photo TODOs against the existing backend mutations or remove the stubs.

title: AppSync 365-day API key with Query.profile(userId:) readable for any user
description: MEDIUM-4: infra/graphql/schema.graphql:156 marks Query.profile(userId: ID!) with @aws_api_key while accepting an arbitrary user id, so any API-key holder can read any user's profile. The additional API_KEY authorization mode at infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:150-160 issues a key valid for 365 days with no rotation story.
recommendation: Remove @aws_api_key from Query.profile; if a public view is needed, expose a separate field returning only non-sensitive fields. Drop the API_KEY auth mode if unused, otherwise shorten the expiry and document rotation.

title: 29 raw console.* calls with no logging abstraction
description: LOW-9: 29 raw console.log/warn/error calls exist across ui/src and infra. ui/.eslintrc.cjs:17-18 only warns on them in production builds, so they are neither removed nor routed through a structured logger, and the Lambda/resolver side produces no correlatable structured output.
recommendation: Introduce a small logging abstraction with levels for the UI and structured JSON logging (with a correlation id) for the Lambda handlers, then raise the no-console rule to error.

title: Four mutually inconsistent JavaScript language baselines
description: LOW-3: Four different JavaScript baselines are declared simultaneously: ui/tsconfig.json:3 (target/module ESNext with legacy moduleResolution: Node), ui/vite.config.ts:14 (build.target es2022, required for the BigInt literals the Cognito SDK emits), ui/.eslintrc.cjs:12 (parserOptions.ecmaVersion 2020, so the linter mis-parses syntax the build emits), and ui/.browserslistrc (Chrome/Edge ≥79, Firefox ≥70, Safari/iOS ≥14 — predating several ES2022 features, and unused because Vite sets build.target explicitly).
recommendation: Standardise on ES2022: set tsconfig target/lib to ES2022 with moduleResolution "bundler", raise the ESLint parser ecmaVersion to 2022, and either align .browserslistrc with ES2022-capable browsers or delete it as dead configuration.

title: Access, ID and refresh tokens stored in localStorage; JWT decoded without verification
description: MEDIUM-10: ui/src/lib/auth/composables/useAuthSession.ts:154-159 persists the access, ID and refresh tokens to localStorage (cleared at :161-171). ui/src/lib/auth/utils/jwt.ts:5-15 decodes the ID token without verifying its signature. Mitigating factors: the app has no XSS sinks, access tokens are short-lived (1 hour) and revocation is enabled; the residual risk is that a future XSS or malicious dependency yields a 30-day refresh token.
recommendation: Stop persisting the refresh token in localStorage — keep access/ID tokens in memory and rely on the Cognito SDK refresh path, or move the refresh token to an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie issued by a backend. Pair with adding a CSP.

title: Dead code and Ionic starter-template leftovers still committed
description: LOW-6: Verified by inbound-reference count across ui/src and ui/tests: ui/src/views/Tab2Page.vue (0 refs), ui/src/views/Tab3Page.vue (0), ui/src/shared/components/LoadingSpinner.vue (0) are unreachable; ui/src/views/Tab1Page.vue (1 ref, only from the placeholder ui/tests/unit/example.spec.ts:2) and ui/src/components/ExploreContainer.vue (3 refs, all from the Tab pages) form a cluster kept alive only by that placeholder test. Also committed: 6 empty .gitkeep files in already-populated directories (ui/src/lib/auth/{components,composables,services,styles,types,utils}/.gitkeep), ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/example.json and ui/.vscode/extensions.json. Note ui/src/config/access.ts is NOT dead — it is imported by ui/src/router/index.ts:6 as featureGates.
recommendation: Delete the unreachable Tab2Page.vue, Tab3Page.vue and LoadingSpinner.vue individually, then remove the Tab1Page/ExploreContainer cluster together with the placeholder spec, and drop the redundant .gitkeep and fixture files.

title: No GraphQL codegen — schema and client documents already drifting
description: MEDIUM-15: infra/graphql/schema.graphql (172 lines, 5 queries + 5 mutations) is hand-maintained and the UI's GraphQL documents are hand-written inline (e.g. exerciseService.ts:36-50) with no codegen step, so there is no compile-time link between schema and client. Drift is already visible: ui/src/features/profile/services/profileService.ts:270 carries "TODO: Implement photo upload when backend endpoint is available" although the endpoint exists (infra/lib/lambda/profile-photo/index.ts plus the requestProfilePhotoUpload/confirmProfilePhotoUpload mutations). A schema comment also documents the sort key as EXERCISE#<id> while the resolvers write EXERCISE#<date>#<id>.
recommendation: Add a GraphQL codegen step producing typed operations from infra/graphql/schema.graphql, consume the generated types in the UI services, and correct the stale schema comment.

title: Privilege escalation: client-writable Cognito `tier` attribute trusted from an unverified JWT claim
description: HIGH-2: infra/lib/constructs/auth.ts:88-94 includes the custom `tier` attribute in the Cognito app client's writeAttributes, so a signed-in user can set their own custom:tier via UpdateUserAttributes. The UI reads the tier from the ID-token claim (ui/src/lib/auth/composables/useAuthSession.ts:138-143) via decodeJwtPayload (ui/src/lib/auth/utils/jwt.ts:5-15), which base64-decodes without verifying the signature and swallows errors. All gates (useAccessTier.ts, TierGate.vue, PremiumFeatureLock.vue, createRouterGuard.ts, router meta.requiredTier) derive from that client-trusted value, so a free-tier user can grant themselves premium access.
recommendation: Remove `tier` from writeAttributes so only an admin/backend path can set it, and enforce tier authorization server-side in AppSync resolvers rather than trusting a client-decoded claim.

title: No CI/CD pipeline and no declared Node runtime version
description: MEDIUM-5: There is no .github/ directory, buildspec.yml, or any pipeline configuration in the repository — every build, lint, test, synth and deploy runs from a developer workstation via Makefile targets, so lint/tests/typecheck are never gated and no dependency or CVE scanning runs. No engines field exists in the root, ui or infra package.json and there is no .nvmrc/.node-version, so the authoritative Node version is undeclared. The infra workspace additionally mixes a Python 3.12 Lambda (infra/lib/constructs/seed-user.ts:67) into an otherwise all-TypeScript project with neither toolchain version declared.
recommendation: Add an engines field and a matching .nvmrc, and add a CI workflow running npm ci, lint, test, build and cdk synth on every pull request with a dependency-audit step. Document or remove the Python toolchain requirement.

title: ionicons 7 pinned while @ionic/vue 8 ships ionicons 8
description: LOW-5: ui/package.json declares ionicons ^7.0.0 (resolved 7.4.0) while @ionic/vue 8.8.19 and @ionic/core ship ionicons 8.1.0 nested, so two major versions of the icon library are installed in the same tree.
recommendation: Raise the ionicons declaration to ^8.0.0 to match @ionic/vue 8, de-duplicating the nested copy, and verify the icon imports still resolve.

title: Outdated dev tooling: @vitejs/plugin-vue, jsdom, cypress
description: LOW-4: Outdated dev tooling in ui/package.json with no known CVEs at the resolved versions: @vitejs/plugin-vue ^4.0.0 (resolved 4.6.2; 5.x is the release paired with Vite 5), jsdom ^22.1.0 (resolved 22.1.0; 25.x+ current), cypress ^13.5.0 (resolved 13.17.0; 15.x current).
recommendation: Bump @vitejs/plugin-vue alongside the Vite upgrade, and update jsdom and cypress to current majors, re-running the unit and e2e suites after each.

title: Service layer has no error handling and no server-side input validation
description: MEDIUM-8: ui/src/features/exercise/services/exerciseService.ts (384 LOC) and ui/src/features/profile/services/profileService.ts (287 LOC) contain zero try/catch blocks; all error handling lives in the Pinia stores (exerciseStore.ts:69,88,107,123; profileStore.ts:29,50,72,90), so any consumer calling a service directly gets unhandled promise rejections. Separately, the eight resolvers in infra/resolvers/ correctly propagate DynamoDB errors but perform no input validation, so every business constraint (duration 1-1440, name length, positive distance) exists only in the browser's zod schemas and can be bypassed by a direct GraphQL call with a valid token. ui/src/lib/auth/utils/jwt.ts:12 silently returns null on any malformed token.
recommendation: Introduce a typed error wrapper so both services return modelled results instead of relying on their caller's store, and add server-side input validation plus distinguishable domain errors in infra/resolvers/*.ts.

title: S3 media bucket CORS allows all origins and all headers
description: MEDIUM-3: infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:111-118 configures the S3 media bucket CORS rule with allowedOrigins: ['*'] and allowedHeaders: ['*'], so any origin can issue presigned PUT requests against the bucket from a browser.
recommendation: Replace the wildcards with the CloudFront distribution domain (plus http://localhost:5173 for development, supplied per environment) and only the headers the presigned PUT needs (content-type, content-length).

title: AppSync fieldLogLevel ALL outside production may log PII
description: LOW-10: infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:162-164 sets AppSync fieldLogLevel: ALL for non-production environments, which writes full request and response bodies — including health-profile PII — to CloudWatch Logs, with no retention bound documented.
recommendation: Lower the non-production field log level to ERROR (or enable ALL only behind an explicit debug flag) and set an explicit log retention period on the AppSync log group.

title: CloudFront has no WAF and no security-headers response policy
description: MEDIUM-11: The CloudFront distribution at infra/lib/constructs/ui-hosting.ts:177-186 has no AWS WAF web ACL associated and no ResponseHeadersPolicy attached, so no Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy header reaches the browser.
recommendation: Attach a ResponseHeadersPolicy supplying CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and associate a WAF web ACL with at least the managed common and known-bad-input rule groups.

title: Zero tests for all of infra/ and all 35 .vue components
description: MEDIUM-6: The entire infra workspace (1,481 LOC across lib/, resolvers/, bin/ and graphql/) has no tests; infra/package.json declares no test runner and its build script is only tsc --noEmit. All 35 .vue components, including the 1,525-LOC CognitoAuth.vue, are untested, and ui/vite.config.ts:23-45 sets coverage include: ['src/**/*.ts'], excluding .vue files entirely. The whole of ui/src/lib/auth/ (cognitoService.ts 435 LOC, useAuthSession, useAccessTier, jwt, createRouterGuard, ...) — the highest-risk security code — is untested, as are ui/src/lib/preferences/, features/discover/ and features/settings/. ui/tests/ is 6 files / 94 LOC of Ionic starter scaffolding: ui/tests/unit/example.spec.ts and ui/tests/e2e/specs/test.cy.ts only assert the literal string 'Tab 1 page'.
recommendation: Add a Vitest project to infra/ with aws-cdk-lib/assertions template tests asserting security-relevant properties (CORS origins, auth modes, writeAttributes, removal policies, Lambda runtime) and unit tests for the eight resolvers. Extend ui coverage include to .vue files and add tests for ui/src/lib/auth/ and the tier-gating components. Replace the placeholder specs with real smoke journeys.

title: vite 5.4.21 has one HIGH and two MEDIUM dev-server CVEs
description: MEDIUM-1: ui/package.json declares vite ^5.0.0, resolved to 5.4.21. A CVE scan reports CVE-2026-53571 (HIGH, server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths), CVE-2026-39365 (MEDIUM, path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling) and CVE-2026-53632 (MEDIUM, launch-editor NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC paths), all fixed by 6.4.3. Exposure is dev-server only (devDependency, not the shipped static bundle), hence Medium.
recommendation: Upgrade vite to >= 6.4.3, coordinating the major bump with @vitejs/plugin-vue 5.x, and re-run the build and test suite.

title: aws-cdk-lib 2.232.1 carries two HIGH command-injection CVEs
description: HIGH-3: infra/package.json pins aws-cdk-lib exactly at 2.232.1 (resolved 2.232.1 in package-lock.json). A CVE scan reports CVE-2026-11417 (HIGH, OS command injection in NodejsFunction bundling, fixed 2.246.0), CVE-2026-13760 (HIGH, OS command injection in NodejsFunction Docker bundling, fixed 2.260.0) and GHSA-464c-974j-9xm6 (LOW, CodeBuild S3 log encryption boolean inversion, fixed 2.253.0). The repository uses exactly the affected construct at infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:124-139.
recommendation: Upgrade aws-cdk-lib to >= 2.260.0 and bump the aws-cdk CLI in step, then re-run cdk synth to confirm no construct API drift.

title: esbuild 0.21.5 transitive under Vite has a dev-server request-forgery advisory
description: MEDIUM-2: package-lock.json resolves esbuild 0.21.5 under node_modules/vite/node_modules/esbuild. GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99 (MEDIUM) allows any website to send requests to the dev server; fixed in 0.25.0. The separately declared infra esbuild ^0.25.0 (resolved 0.25.12) is not affected.
recommendation: Resolve by upgrading vite to a version that depends on esbuild >= 0.25.0, or add an npm override pinning esbuild >= 0.25.0.

title: Releases accumulate forever; destructive removal policies keyed on a free-text string
description: MEDIUM-12: infra/lib/constructs/ui-hosting.ts:205-207 deploys with prune: false and retainOnDelete: true and no S3 lifecycle rule, so every release ever deployed remains under releases/<id>/ indefinitely. Conversely infra/lib/constructs/api.ts:120-121, ui-hosting.ts:160-161 and the user pool in auth.ts set removalPolicy: DESTROY with autoDeleteObjects: !isProd, where isProd derives from a free-text `environment` context string validated only against a three-element list in infra/bin/app.ts:10-15 — so any environment not named exactly 'production' is treated as disposable, including its Cognito user pool and DynamoDB table.
recommendation: Add an S3 lifecycle rule expiring old release prefixes, and key removal/auto-delete policies on an explicit, validated enum (or an explicit retain flag) rather than an exact free-text match on 'production'.

title: CognitoAuth.vue is a 1,525-LOC component holding four auth modes
description: MEDIUM-7: ui/src/lib/auth/components/CognitoAuth.vue is 1,525 LOC containing all four auth modes (sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, confirm) in one single-file component, with 9 `any` occurrences and no tests. Its styling lives separately in the 555-LOC ui/src/lib/auth/styles/cognito-auth.css. Other oversized files: cognitoService.ts (435), exerciseService.unit.test.ts (431), exerciseService.ts (384), profileService.unit.test.ts (316), with ten more in the 260-300 LOC band including infra/lib/constructs/api.ts (265) and PreferencesPanel.vue (297).
recommendation: Split CognitoAuth.vue into one component per auth mode over the shared useCognitoAuth composable, co-locate the mode-specific CSS, and add tests per extracted component — after a test harness exists so the split is verifiable.

title: Two AppSync resolver runtimes maintained side by side
description: LOW-12: infra/lib/constructs/api.ts wires most fields through a VTL `vtlResolver` helper (:175+) while `myPreferences` uses the APPSYNC_JS runtime (:210-216), so two resolver languages must be maintained for a single API — contributors need both VTL and JS resolver knowledge, and the eight VTL templates in infra/resolvers/ share no code with the JS one.
recommendation: Standardise on the APPSYNC_JS runtime for all resolvers (it also enables unit testing), converting the eight VTL templates, or keep VTL only and move myPreferences back to it.
